messages:
alex: heads up — ran a ~24h run of the TP+PP config with fused/flash-attn on 8xA100. seeing recurring latency spikes around step ~1200 that line up with big all-gather windows. overall throughput ok but jitter kills p95. anyone seen this pattern?

maya: quick q — is this with qkv all-gather enabled or using qkv scatter?

alex: qkv_allgather=auto (runtime picks gather), flash_attn=enabled, tp=2, pp=4. profiler snippet attached below. spikes correspond to "all_gather_qkv" entries.

jin: can you paste the profiler lines? small ones are easier to parse. :eyes:

alex: sure — raw lines from perf collector:
```
[perf] step=1196 tokens=4096 compute_ms=16 comm_ms=12 all_gather_q_ms=3 all_gather_kv_ms=28 flash_fallback=false
[perf] step=1197 tokens=4096 compute_ms=15 comm_ms=48 all_gather_q_ms=6 all_gather_kv_ms=37 flash_fallback=true
[perf] step=1198 tokens=4096 compute_ms=17 comm_ms=52 all_gather_q_ms=7 all_gather_kv_ms=40 flash_fallback=true
```

maya: that jump in all_gather_kv_ms + flash_fallback=true is suspicious. when flash falls back we lose kernel-level overlap and comm balloons. where is the fallback coming from? alignment/padding?

sam: on TP, qkv layout gets chunked differently per rank. flash-attn has strict memory layout assumptions; with scatter/gather we sometimes hit an incompatible stride and runtime drops to safe kernel. try forcing flash_attn=force (if available) or enabling a small padding tolerance.

alex: tried force -> crash on some sequence lengths (index OOB in fused kernel), so force isn't safe. auto selects fallback which causes the runtime to serialize more collectives.

jin: two ideas: 1) relax kernel selection so that fused kernel picks a slower but TP-friendly path (reduces fallback). 2) overlap strategy — start all-gather for KV earlier and prefetch into host pinned buffer while compute runs. do we have traces showing comm/compute overlap?

alex: yes attached a trace flame. compute blocks were not overlapped during the fallback. here's a tiny ascii timeline:
```
step 1197: |compute(15ms)|--wait--|all-gather(37ms)|
non-fallback: |compute(15ms) + overlap|all-gather(12ms overlapped)|
```

maya: can you repro with nvprof/nsys and collect NCCL traces? if NCCL shows barrier at all-gather start times we can confirm synchronization points.

alex: scheduled an nsys capture for tonight. also logged NCCL times:
```
NCCL: allReduce_total_ms=48, allReduce_avg_ms=12, allGather_qkv_ms=36 (rank skewed)
```

sam: another angle — KV cache behavior. when cache grows we sometimes switch to a different memory layout (sharded vs replicated) across steps leading to extra comm metadata sync. did cache size change around step 1200?

alex: yes step 1200 coincides with longer sequences entering the batch (we had an overflow batch with padding), so kv cache shards rebalanced. that might explain the extra metadata exchange before real KV all-gather.

jin: ok that gives us a reproducible trigger: 1) mixed sequence length causing pad+rebalance, 2) runtime selects qkv gather that produces a stride incompatible with fused kernel -> fallback, 3) fallback prevents comm/compute overlap -> all-gather becomes visible in p95.

maya: perf experiment plan: A) force uniform seq-len padding to avoid rebalance; B) change kernel selection heuristics to prefer TP-friendly fused kernel when rebalancing expected; C) implement lightweight prefetch of KV shards to reduce metadata sync. any objections?

alex: plan A repro'd locally and p95 improved from 420ms -> 290ms. plan B needs runtime touch. I can prototype a duck-typed kernel selection flag: prefer_tp_friendly=true.

sam: small note — prefer_tp_friendly may increase steady-state compute (10-12%) but reduce jitter. document tradeoff in optimize suggestions.

perf-bot: perf-alert: when running 8xA100 tp=2 pp=4 flash_attn=enabled, observed 31% p95 regression on job/2026-03-15-08 compared to baseline-run/2026-03-01-21.

jin: thanks perf-bot. alex, if you can push prototype config, I can add a quick microbenchmark harness to test various kernel choices with synthetic KV sizes.

alex: will push a branch later today (branch: runtime/tp-fused-kernel-heuristic). includes a config flag and extra logging for qkv stride detection.

maya: also add a runtime metric for "flash_fallback_count" so we can alert on rising fallback rates in production.

alex: good call — added to the branch TODOs.

sam: takeaway for doc: when mixing TP with fused-attn, watch QKV layout skew during variable-length batches; prefer deterministic padding or runtime heuristics that trade compute for stable comm/overlap. add to internal perf playbook. :memo:

alex: agree. will post follow-up thread with benchmark results and PR link once nsys traces are in. thanks all. :thumbsup:
